resources.string: Lets TVRelay detect when you select a movie or show recommendation on the launcher, so it can open it in Nuvio or Stremio instead.

TVRelay uses an Accessibility Service to detect when you click a movie or show recommendation on your TV's home screen. When it does, it sends only that title's text to TheTVDB to identify it, then shows a "Watch now" button for the app you've chosen in Settings - tapping it (and only tapping it) opens that title there, so an accidental click never jumps you into another app on its own.

Nothing else is read, collected, or sent anywhere. Every other click (apps, menus, anything that isn't a content recommendation) is left completely alone.

You can turn the service off at any time from this app's Settings.
Pick which app opens when you select a recommendation on your TV\'s home screen.
Status: not enabled - select to open system settings
Status: enabled - a confirm button appears before opening another app
Status: not enabled - recognized clicks open the app directly with no confirmation. Select to grant \"display over other apps\"

If you sideloaded this app and the Accessibility toggle switches itself back off right after you enable it: that's Android's "Restricted settings" protection for apps not installed from an app store, not a bug. Look for "Allow restricted setting" on this app's system App info screen. If you can't find it, connect over ADB and run:

adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.hmartinez94.tvrelay/com.hmartinez94.tvrelay.TvRelayAccessibilityService
adb shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1

(The first command replaces the whole list - separate services with a colon if you already use another one, like TalkBack.)

Some recommendation cards don\'t expose their title to accessibility tools, so TVRelay can\'t always detect them automatically. Type the title here instead - everything after that (looking it up, opening your chosen app) works exactly the same way.

Whichever service TVRelay asks to identify a clicked title. TheTVDB is the default and needs nothing from you. TMDB is an alternative if TheTVDB ever gives you a wrong match for a title - it requires your own free personal API key (get one at themoviedb.org, under Settings → API), used only for your own lookups and subject to TMDB\'s terms of use.
